meta.title_plain: How Andy Roddick's rocket serve took him to world No. 1
meta.teaser: Roddick almost quit at 17, then won the 2003 US Open and reached No. 1.

page.title: How Andy Roddick's rocket serve took him to world No. 1
page.bigIdea: Roddick nearly quit tennis at 17. Four more months of hard work turned him into the best junior in the world, then a US Open champion.

cards.title: The little brother
cards.front: Andy was born in Omaha, USA, in 1982. He was the youngest of three boys.
cards.back: His big brother John was a top junior, ranked as high as No. 6 in the world. Andy wanted to keep up with him.
cards.tryit: Pick a player you look up to. Copy one of their habits in practice this week.

cards.title: Four more months
cards.front: At 17, Roddick lost a lot of junior matches in a row. He thought about quitting.
cards.back: His coach, Tarik Benhabiles, asked for four more months of full focus. In 2000, Andy became the world's No. 1 junior.
cards.tryit: Choose one shot that feels stuck. Practise only that shot for 15 minutes.

cards.title: A serve like a rocket
cards.front: Roddick's serve was short, snappy and super fast. Strong legs powered it.
cards.back: He once served at 152 mph, about 245 km/h, in a Grand Slam. He hit over 9,000 aces in his career.
cards.tryit: Serve 10 balls. Bend your knees and push up with your legs on each one.

cards.title: Two sets down, then champion
cards.front: In the 2003 US Open semifinal, he lost the first two sets and faced match point.
cards.back: He saved it with a big serve and won. In the final he beat Juan Carlos Ferrero, finishing with three aces in a row.
cards.tryit: Play a practice game where you start at 15-40. Try to win it anyway.

cards.title: Winning for his team
cards.front: At age 10, Roddick watched the USA win the Davis Cup. He dreamed of doing it too.
cards.back: In 2007 he did it, with James Blake and the Bryan brothers. When he could clinch a tie, he won all 12 times.
cards.tryit: Play doubles with a friend. Say one encouraging thing after every point.

words.d: A serve so good the other player can't even touch it.
A point where one player wins the whole match if they win it.
A team competition where countries play each other in tennis.
One of tennis's four biggest tournaments, like Wimbledon or the US Open.
The player ranked best in the world when the season ends.

quiz.q: What did Roddick's coach ask him to do when he wanted to quit?
opts: Give tennis four more months of full focus
quiz.hint: Look at card 2. It was a short, clear deal.
quiz.why: Benhabiles asked for four focused months, and Roddick became junior world No. 1 in 2000.

quiz.hint: Think about the word 'ace' and card 3.
quiz.why: His fast serve won him free points, with over 9,000 aces in his career.

quiz.q: What happened in his 2003 US Open semifinal?
opts: He won in three easy sets
He came back from two sets down and a match point
quiz.why: He was two sets down and faced match point, but fought back to win in five sets.

quiz.q: Why did winning the 2007 Davis Cup mean so much to Roddick?
opts: It was his first match ever
It was played in his backyard
He'd dreamed of it since watching the USA win as a kid
quiz.hint: Go back to when he was 10 years old.
quiz.why: He watched the USA win the Davis Cup in 1992 and helped them win it again in 2007.

page.think: Roddick almost quit, then gave it four more months. What's one thing you'd give four focused months to get better at?
tries: Spend 15 minutes on serves, using your legs to push up
Watch highlights of the 2003 US Open final and count Roddick's aces
Play one game starting at 15-40 and try to fight back
Tell Dad one idea from this report
